chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ibrahim ibn Salih, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The pilgrim (for Hajj) and the pilgrim (for Umra) are the delegates of Allah. If they ask Him, He grants them; and if they supplicate to Him, He answers them; and if they intercede, He accepts their intercession; and if they are silent, He initiates (bestowing upon them); and they are compensated with one Dirham for a thousand (and a) thousand Dirhams.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَم: Dirham (a unit of currency used here for compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status and reward of pilgrims according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi elevates the pilgrim to the status of 'Wafd Allah' (delegates of God), a concept rooted in the Prophetic tradition that grants them a unique proximity to the Divine. The Imam emphasizes that their status is so honored that even their silence is met with proactive divine favor, reflecting the comprehensive mercy associated with the sacred rites of Hajj and Umra. This spiritual compensation is often interpreted by scholars as both a metaphor for immense spiritual reward and a literal promise of sustenance, underscoring the transformative power of these pilgrimages.
